transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I just don’t care about anything anymore. It’s not even one specific thing, it’s like everything that used to feel like “me” has gone flat. I used to take art classes, and I actually loved them—I’d get excited about colors and projects and staying late to finish something—but now I can’t make myself go, and even thinking about it just feels like too much.

And my friends do board-game nights, which used to be this really nice routine, like snacks and joking around and arguing over rules, and now I just… don’t go. I don’t even feel the pull to go. Hiking too—I used to like being outside, having somewhere to go, feeling my body move—but lately I just stay in my room. I keep telling myself I should try to get back to the soccer team too, because that used to matter to me, but I don’t care enough to do anything about it.

It feels like I’m sitting there watching everything slip away, and I know I should care, but I don’t. That’s what scares me, I think. Not that I’m sad about one thing, but that I’m just… not interested in my own life.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yes… most days. It’s hard to explain because it’s not always like I’m crying or having some obvious breakdown, but I wake up and there’s this heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. Like before I even open my eyes all the way, I already feel like the day is over somehow.

It’s this sense that there isn’t really a future for me beyond the apartment walls. I know that sounds dramatic, but that’s how it feels—like everything outside is still happening, people are going places and making plans and living, and I’m just… stuck in this small space with this weight in me. And it’s there most of the day, nearly every day. It doesn’t really lift much.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or lack energy most of the time, even when you haven't done much physically?

Yes. All the time, honestly. It’s not even the kind of tired where I can point to a reason, like, “Oh, I had a busy day,” because most days I haven’t done much at all. I can be in bed for half the day, not really doing anything, and then the smallest thing feels impossible.

Like taking a shower sounds simple, but when I think about getting up, getting towels, standing there, washing my hair… it feels like this huge project. And answering one message on my phone can feel like I’ve already worked a full shift, which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, but that’s really what it feels like. I’ll look at a text and know it would take maybe thirty seconds, and still my body reacts like it’s too much.

It’s like my energy is already gone before I even start anything.
Have you found that you no longer take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even activities you really liked before, like art or time with friends?

Yes… definitely. That’s probably the part that makes me feel the most unlike myself, honestly. It’s not just that I’m too tired to do things — it’s like the part of me that used to want them is gone.

Art classes used to be a big thing for me. I’d look forward to them, I’d think about what I wanted to make, I’d get kind of absorbed in it. And now even picturing myself walking into the room, setting things up, trying to care about a project… it just feels blank. Like there’s no spark there.

And with my friends, the board-game nights used to be something I really liked. I liked the routine of it, being around people, laughing, having something normal to do. Now I just stay in my room instead. Sometimes I’ll see the messages about it and I know I should answer or go, but I don’t feel anything pulling me toward it.

Same with hiking, and even soccer. I keep thinking maybe I should get back to the team, because it used to matter to me, but I can’t get myself to care enough to actually do it. It feels like I’m just watching all these parts of my life slip away, and I’m sitting there letting it happen. I know I should care more, but I just… don’t.
Have you been feeling like you’re worthless or that you’ve let yourself or others down in some way, more than you normally would?

Yes… a lot. More than I even want to admit, because once I start saying it out loud it sounds so ugly, but it’s there all the time.

I keep replaying things I did wrong, especially in my marriage. Like I’ll be sitting there and suddenly I’m back in some argument, remembering the exact thing I said, or the way I shut down, or the times I wasn’t loving in the way I should’ve been. And it’s not like a normal regret where you think, “I wish I handled that better.” It turns into this whole… proof, I guess, that I ruin things. That I hurt people just by being close to them.

And with my friends too. I keep thinking about every message I didn’t answer, every time I cancelled, every time I made things awkward or needed too much. I’ll go over tiny moments again and again, like maybe they were signs that I was selfish or draining or just not worth the effort. Even if someone else would probably say it wasn’t a big deal, in my head it feels like this huge list of evidence against me.

Sometimes I honestly feel like people would be safer if I wasn’t around. Not safer like… I don’t know how to say it without sounding alarming, but safer from having to deal with me. Less burdened. Like their lives would be lighter if I were gone, because then they wouldn’t have to worry about me or be disappointed in me anymore. I know that’s a horrible thing to think, but it feels true when I’m in it.
Has there been a time recently when even things that used to bring you joy, like art or spending time outdoors, felt completely empty or meaningless to you?

Yes. That’s kind of why I’m here, honestly. It feels like I don’t care about anything anymore, and I don’t mean that in a dramatic way, like I’m just having a bad week or I’m bored. It’s more like the feeling has been scraped out of everything.

Art classes used to feel like… I don’t know, like one of the few places where I could still recognize myself. Even if I wasn’t great or I was messy, I cared. I wanted to make something. Now I think about going and it just feels pointless. Like I can imagine sitting there with the supplies in front of me and I already feel empty before I even start.

And board-game nights with my friends used to be something I actually looked forward to. Same with hiking, being outside, even just having that sense of air and space. Now I mostly just sit in my room. I know those things are still happening, like life is still going on outside the door, but I don’t feel connected to any of it.

Even soccer… I keep telling myself I should try to get back to the team, because there was a time when that mattered to me. But now the thought comes up and then just disappears, because there’s no pull behind it. No excitement, no real reason that feels strong enough.

It’s like I’m watching everything slip away and I’m just sitting there letting it happen. And the worst part is I know those things used to bring me joy, so I can tell something is really wrong, but I still can’t make myself feel anything about them.
Have you been feeling this way — with a depressed mood or loss of interest in things — for most of the day, more days than not, for the past two years or more?

Not two years, no. It feels like forever when I’m in it, so part of me wants to say yes, but if I actually count it out, the really constant part started around the following summer.

Before that, I think there were stretches where I was low or I’d lose interest for a while, but it wasn’t like this all the time. Around that summer it kind of settled in and stopped lifting, if that makes sense. Since then it’s been most days, most of the day — like the default setting became depressed or empty instead of just having episodes of feeling bad.

So… about a year and four months now, I think. Not quite two years, but long enough that it doesn’t feel temporary anymore.

Have you ever experienced periods where your mood was elevated, expansive, or unusually irritable, along with increased energy or activity, lasting at least several days and representing a noticeable change from your usual behavior?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean… I know I’ve had times where I was irritable, definitely, but when you say “elevated” or “expansive,” I don’t know if I’ve ever thought of myself that way.

There have been times when people might say I seemed different, maybe more keyed up or harder to be around, but I don’t know if it lasted several days in the way you mean, or if it was just me reacting to stress or not sleeping well or getting overwhelmed. I have a hard time separating those things out. Like, if I’m agitated for a few days, is that what you mean? Or does it have to feel good, like confident and energized? Because I don’t really remember it feeling good.

I don’t think I’ve had a clear stretch where I was suddenly full of energy and doing a lot more than usual and everyone would say, “Wow, this is not like you,” but I also don’t trust my memory completely with that kind of thing. I mostly remember the low parts more clearly. So… I guess my answer is I’m not sure. I haven’t noticed anything that I would confidently describe that way.
Do you often wake up earlier than you intend to, and find it difficult to go back to sleep, even if you haven’t gotten enough rest?

Yes. That happens a lot. It’s not even just that I wake up early — it’s the whole night kind of goes wrong before that.

I’ll lie there for hours, and I keep getting up to check the door. I’ll tell myself I already checked it, but then I’ll hear something, or think I heard something, and I have to listen again. So I’m awake, just staring and listening, and it feels like my body won’t actually settle down enough to sleep.

Then when I finally do fall asleep, it’s like I don’t stay under very long. I wake up before dawn, sometimes shaking, and once I’m awake it’s basically over. I can’t get back to sleep, even if I know I’ve barely slept. I’ll just lie there exhausted, but still too keyed up to drop off again.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Yeah… I have. I don’t really notice hunger the same way lately, or maybe I ignore it until it’s not even there anymore. Most days I’ll get through almost the whole day without eating anything real. It’s not like I’m trying to diet or anything — food just seems… pointless? Like I’ll look at something I normally would’ve eaten and it’s like cardboard in my mouth, or even just the thought of chewing it feels like too much effort.

And then I’ll realize it’s late and I’ve had maybe a few bites of something, or coffee, or nothing much at all. I know that sounds bad when I say it out loud.

I haven’t been weighing myself consistently, so I don’t know the exact number, but my clothes are definitely different. My jeans have gotten really loose — like, loose enough that I’ve had to knot the waistband to keep them up because they slide around. That was kind of the thing that made me realize it wasn’t just in my head. I wasn’t trying to lose weight, it just… happened because I’m not eating much.
